title: Renewal Flag & Salvage Roadmap
body:
Purpose:
This playbook is an early-warning + salvage roadmap for renewals that are showing first- and second-order risk signals. It prioritizes speed: detect, triage, stabilize, escalate, and attempt save within a 30-day sprint window. Meant for CSMs, AMs, and CS leadership.

Audience and intent:
- Primary: Customer Success Managers (CSMs) owning accounts between 50k-2M ARR.
- Secondary: Solutions Eng, Renewals Ops, Sales execs, and Product liaisons when product regressions are implicated.
- Intent: Provide prescriptive actions and templated artifacts to reduce churn probability and create a clear exec escalation path when needed.

When to use this doc (triggers):
Use the roadmap when any of the following are observed in the trailing 90 days:
- Monthly usage falls by >= 30% month-over-month for two consecutive months.
- NPS or CSAT drops below 30 for key contacts AND an open support ticket with severity >= 2 remains unresolved >5 days.
- Customer indicates renewal hesitation in a QBR or key stakeholder has not responded to outreach for 3+ weeks.
- A product regression causes a production-impacting incident with customer-facing SLAs violated.
- Contract value at risk >= $50k ARR AND there is an upcoming renewal within 120 days.

Risk scorecard (fast triage matrix):
Assign points and sum to get a risk score (0-30). High risk >= 16, Medium 8-15, Low <8.
- Usage drop: 0 (none) / 4 (10-29%) / 8 (>=30%)
- Support churn signals: 0 / 3 (one Sev2/3 recent) / 6 (repeated Sev2 or Sev1)
- Stakeholder engagement: 0 / 3 (one non-responsive stakeholder) / 6 (multiple)
- Financial exposure: 0 / 3 (<$50k ARR) / 6 (>=$50k ARR)
- Strategic importance: 0 / 2 (non-strategic) / 4 (integrated into product roadmap)
- Contract runway: 0 / 2 (>120 days) / 4 (<=120 days)

Three-tiered response plays (play priority and owner):
1) Cooling & Stabilize (CSM lead, timeline day 0-7):
  - Immediate health-call within 48 hours; single-sheet health summary sent in advance.
  - Triage support backlog with SRE/Support: escalate any Sev>=2 to hot path and assign an ETA.
  - Quick-win checklist: usage causes, config drift, API keys/credentials, rate-limits, billing disputes.
  - Offer short-term remediation credits (PS hours or credit for next invoice) if outage caused by Redwood.
  - Deliverable: 1-page status update (owner: CSM).

2) Repair & Reassure (CSM + Solutions Eng, timeline day 3-14):
  - Run a focused root-cause analysis if product/regression implicated; include timeline and mitigation steps.
  - Propose a stabilization plan with concrete SLAs and owner commitments (SRE, product PM).
  - Re-engage executive sponsor on customer side if risk score >= 16.
  - Offer targeted enablement (training session, playbook review, or on-site/remote workshop).
  - Deliverable: stabilization plan and remediation timeline posted to shared drive and sent to stakeholders.

3) Salvage & Negotiate (Renewals Ops + Sales exec involvement, timeline day 7-30):
  - Execute commercial save options (see save play menu below).
  - Run a 14-day accelerated QBR focused on outcomes and ROI tied to the customer's use cases.
  - If unwilling to renew, negotiate short-term bridge contract (3-6 months) with remediation clauses and a fall-back support SLA.
  - Deliverable: proposed renewal commercial package and exec escalation memo.

Save play menu (pick 1-2 based on exposure):
- PS credit: Offer 10-30 hours of professional services towards onboarding/automation improvements.
- Time-limited discount: 10-20% off ARR for year 1 if customer commits within 14 days.
- Feature roadmap guarantee: prioritized engineering backlog slot + quarterly technical check-ins.
- Performance guarantee: if latency or availability targets missed, apply invoice credit per SLO table.
- Co-funded POC: 50/50 cost share for a measurable expansion pilot tied to new use cases.

Executive escalation protocol (when to escalate up):
Escalate to CS Director when: risk score >= 16 OR contract runway <= 60 days AND unresolved technical or commercial blocker after 7 days.
Escalate to VP CS + Sales Director when: risk score >= 20 OR ARR at risk >= $250k OR customer requests executive-to-executive meeting.
Escalate to CRO/CEO only when: strategic logo at immediate risk (> $1M ARR) OR legal/press exposure.

Escalation packet template (one-pager):
- Subject: Exec Escalation: <Account> — Risk Score <#> — Renewal <date>
- TL;DR (1-2 sentences): current state and ask from execs
- Scorecard snapshot: risk score breakdown and ARR at risk
- Key events (timeline last 30 days)
- Actions taken and outstanding blockers (owners + ETAs)
- Proposed commercial/technical remediation (options and recommendation)
- Immediate ask of execs (e.g., join meeting, approve credit, commit to roadmap slot)
- Attachments: QBR slide excerpts, recent support tickets, SLO incident report

Templates (copy-paste + edit):
1) Slack DM to Sales Dir (CSM -> Sales Dir):
  "Heads-up: <Account> just hit risk score <#>. Usage down 42% MoM, Sev2 incident 10 days unresolved. I need your support for short-term commercial approval (discount/PS credit) and an intro to account exec. Full packet in the escalation folder: <link>. Can you hop on a 20-min sync today?"

2) Email to customer exec (post-stabilization):
  Subject: Next steps on <Product> stability + renewal timeline
  Hi <Name>,
  Thanks for taking the call today. We appreciate the transparency and want to be explicit about our commitments: 1) we will remediate the issue by <date>; 2) we are proposing <PS hours / credit / discount> as a gesture of goodwill; 3) we would like to schedule an outcome-focused QBR for week of <date>.
  Please let me know if that timeline works or if you prefer a different cadence.
  Best,
  <CSM name>

Operational checklists (quick reference):
- Day 0 (detect): record risk score in renewal tracker, open escalation folder in drive, alert Support and Solutions Eng.
- Day 2: health-call completed, support priority assigned, stabilization owner named.
- Day 7: stabilization plan delivered; if unresolved and score>=16, escalate to CS Director.
- Day 14: salvage commercial package drafted; schedule exec briefing if necessary.
- Day 30: final renewal decision window — either renew, bridge, or churn. Document lessons learned.

Metrics to track for each play:
- Time to first response (target <24h)
- Time to stabilization plan (target <7 days)
- Reduction in risk score after 14 days (target >=50% for salvageable accounts)
- Conversion rate for offers (bridge or renewed contract)
- ARR retained post-play over 12 months

Knowledge handoff and postmortem: 
If a renewal is lost or salvaged, run a 1-hour postmortem within 10 business days. Include CSM, Sales, Solutions Eng, Support lead, and a product PM if product issues were causal. Capture root cause, preventive measures (process, product, or billing), and required playbook updates.

Quick links and artifacts to populate when initiating a play:
- QBR slides (latest): attach export to folder
- Last 12 months usage report: export from analytics
- Support ticket log: link to ticketing system filtered by account
- ARR and contract terms: copy of contract and renewal dates
- Prior executive commit emails: add to attachments

Versioning and feedback loop: 
- Playbook version: v0.9 (draft)
- Submit feedback to the CS playbook tracker (Confluence link in linked_artifacts). We will iterate monthly during the pilot phase.

Appendix: sample stabilization one-pager (example content)
- Account: <Account>
- Risk score: <#>
- Current impact: usage -42% MoM; 2 Sev2 incidents in last 30 days; renewal in 78 days
- Immediate actions: hotfix deploy scheduled by SRE for <date>; customer training scheduled; 10 PS hours offered
- Ask from execs: approve 15% discount for year 1 OR approve 20 PS hours to accelerate automation

Notes to CSMs (practical tips):
- Move fast; keep all comms in the single escalation folder to avoid fragmenting context.
- Keep offers measurable and tied to outcomes (e.g., "we'll reduce your model latency by X%"), not vague goodwill promises.
- Avoid over-discounting: prioritize PS/time-bound credits before top-line discounts.

Contact matrix (owners):
- CSM: primary owner of play (example owner assigned in metadata)
- Solutions Eng: technical remediation owner
- Support/SRE: incident remediation and SLO ownership
- Renewals Ops: commercial packaging and contract changes
- CS Director: first-line exec escalation

End of document.

Document history:
- 2025-11-12: created by Maya Thompson (initial draft)
- 2026-01-07: added risk scoring and save menu (Diego Alvarez)
- 2026-02-28: updated escalation thresholds and timelines (Priya Natarajan)
